With 11/12 LT slots occupied and the portfolio sitting at -75.91% cumulative, I need to free capital from losers that aren't working and redeploy into names with cleaner setups. Selling here at $123.06 crystallizes the -7.3% loss but avoids the tail risk of a stop-out at $115.99 on a gap down. Proceeds of ~$985 returned to cash.

INTC is down 5.3% from entry at $116.27, sitting at $110.12 with a stop at $101.49. That's $8.63 of remaining downside — a further 7.8% drop — before the stop triggers. INTC has been a structural underperformer versus the semis complex: NVDA in this same book is up 25.6% while INTC continues to drift. In a bull regime, holding a semi name with negative momentum and a deteriorating relative-strength profile is an opportunity cost problem. Exiting 4 shares at $110.12 for ~$440, closing the slot, and keeping capital available for a higher-conviction reentry or a new name that clears the bar.

With two slots freed, MSFT at $429.66 is the cleanest large-cap growth entry available. Trading above its SMA50 in a confirmed bull regime, MSFT offers the AI/cloud secular tailwind that has been driving the QQQ's outperformance (QQQ $737 vs SMA50 $665 — a 10.8% spread). Target $520, representing a 21% move and approximately 1.75:1 R/R against the $51.56 stop risk. This fills one of the two freed slots and gives the book a high-quality mega-cap compounder alongside the existing NVDA and META tech exposure.

MSFT is trading at $379.05 against a trailing stop of $378.10 — we are literally one bad tick away from a forced exit. Taking the loss now at $379.05 versus $378.10 saves pennies but more importantly it's a conscious decision to exit a broken position rather than a reactive one. trade_log.signal: Regime invalidation — swing entry predicated on Bull regime large-cap quality
trade_log.reasoning: This position was entered on a Bull regime signal and the regime has since deteriorated to Bear (-3/5). MSFT is already down 3.2% from entry at $390.86, now trading $378.36, with the stop at $371.13 — only $7.23 or 1.9% of cushion remaining. The original thesis (large-cap quality in a bull tape) is no longer valid. Holding a bearish-regime swing trade with shrinking stop cushion and no near-term catalyst to revive it is not a defensible position. The R/R is broken: TP at $437.54 requires a +15.7% rally from here in a market where SPY can't clear its SMA50 at $744. Closing the position, crystallizing the -3.2% loss, and recovering the ~$2,270 back into cash is the right call. The stop exists to protect capital, but regime invalidation overrides — we don't wait for the stop to be hit mechanically when the original setup is clearly dead.

C is trading at $127.65 with a trailing stop sitting at $126.86 — we're 79 cents, less than 0.6%, from a forced exit. In a Bear regime with financials under macro pressure, the asymmetry here is ugly: we're risking the entire position stopping out in a single bad tick while holding only 4 shares with a 42.9% embedded gain. Trimming 2 shares at $127.65 locks in a portion of that gain and reduces the binary risk of a full stop-out on noise. The remaining 2 shares stay in with the stop intact to capture any further upside, but we're not letting a 42.9% winner turn into a fire-sale exit because we held a full lot 62 cents above the stop.

C is trading at $127.11 against a trailing stop of $126.86 — we are 25 cents from a mandatory exit and the bid could touch that level in any tick. With the book down 76% cumulative and a bear regime confirmed, I'm not giving a financial name the benefit of the doubt at this proximity. Financials are historically the first to crack when credit conditions tighten in a bear tape. Locking in the +42.3% gain on 2 shares ($75.62 realized P&L) before the stop takes us out on a gap. The risk of riding this through a potential breakdown at $126 outweighs any incremental upside.

NVDA at $210.78 in a confirmed bull tape with VIX 16.2 and SPY holding above SMA50 $745 and SMA200 $698. At 11 shares, notional is $2,318.58 — roughly 0.97% of portfolio, well within the 10% max. META at $583.63 is a high-conviction large-cap name in a bull regime. 4 shares = $2,334.52 notional, ~0.97% of portfolio. Stop $554.45 (5% below), target $653.67 (12% above), 2.4:1 R/R. META has been a consistent outperformer in risk-on environments, and with the QQQ above SMA50 and VIX subdued, the setup is clean. AMZN at $277.61, 8 shares = $2,220.88 notional, ~0.93% of portfolio. Stop $263.73 (5% below entry), target $310.92 (12% above), 2.4:1 R/R. Adding AMZN diversifies the swing book away from pure semis and social — cloud/consumer cycle exposure in a bull regime where macro is supportive. Three distinct swing names keeps correlation risk manageable and fills 3 of 5 swing slots without concentrating.

MSFT at $495.38 with SPY pressing all-time highs and QQQ $722 clearing SMA50 at $715 — large-cap software is the next leg if semis (NVDA) are already moving. 4 shares = $1,981, roughly 0.8% of portfolio, well inside the 10% cap. No earnings imminent in the near term that would create gap risk.

AAPL at $310.09 — with STRONG_BULL confirmed and 9 long-term slots still open, adding a quality compounder here makes structural sense. 7 shares = $2,171, under 1% of portfolio, keeping cash well above the 10% floor ($218k cash, $2.2k spend leaves ~$216k, still 90%+ cash). AAPL's consumer hardware and services mix provides diversification from the healthcare (WELL) and staples (KO) already in the LT book, and it's the only mega-cap consumer tech name we don't own in any sleeve. At $378.52, a 5% stop lands at $359.59 and a 12% TP targets $424.00 for roughly 2.4:1 R/R. 6 shares at $378.52 = $2,271 notional, well within the 10% cap ($23,975). trade_log.reasoning: LLY at $1,114 is the dominant GLP-1 franchise with a multi-year growth runway. GOOGL at $359 is the cleanest large-cap tech name not already in the book. Strong Bull regime at 5/5, QQQ clearing SMA50 at $715, and we have a slot open in swing. Fills out our tech exposure alongside NVDA, META, AMZN, MSFT without adding redundant single-name risk — GOOGL has distinct ad/cloud revenue drivers versus the pure semiconductor or social plays already on.

AVGO at $418.52 fits the LT book as a semiconductor infrastructure compounder — distinct from NVDA's GPU concentration and complements LLY's defensive biotech anchor. Five shares = $2,093, modest initial position. Trailing stop set 12% below entry at $368.30. Strong Bull regime, VIX at 16.2, and AVGO's AI networking tailwinds give this a multi-month thesis. We have 6 LT slots remaining and need to put dry powder to work systematically while the regime is supportive. This opens a position we can add to on pullbacks.

trade_log.signal: Underperformer trim — weakest risk/reward in swing book
trade_log.reasoning: AMZN is down 2.3% from entry at $277.75 and is the weakest name in the swing book. This frees a marginal amount of mental capital and actual cash without fully abandoning the thesis.
